questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are notes. Some notes are cheques. All cheques are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are loans.
II. No notes is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few accounts are notes. All notes are cheques. No cheques is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are not notes.
II. No notes is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some accounts are notes. All notes are cheques. No cheques is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some accounts are cheques.
II. Some notes are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No accounts is a notes. Some notes are cheques. All cheques are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All accounts are loans.
II. Some loans are notes.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: P < R > Q < W > S.
Conclusions: I. W > R   II. Q < S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth access secure = ze ni to
growth banking rural = vo to pa
access banking digital = mi vo ze
secure rural digital = pa ni mi
growth access digital = mi ze to
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: to. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = to, access = ze, secure = ni, banking = vo, rural = pa, digital = mi.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 15 km east, turns left and walks 16 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20. Net displacement is 12 km east and 16 km north. By Pythagoras, √(12² + 16²) = 20 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 34 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 4 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 18 km east, turns left and walks 12 km, then turns left and walks 9 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Net displacement is 9 km east and 12 km north. By Pythagoras, √(9² + 12²) = 15 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of B. F is the daughter of B. G is the father of B. How is F related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. G is a parent of B, and F is B’s daughter. Hence F is G’s grandchild.

questions.stem: H is the brother of C. C is the mother of E. B is the father of H and C. How is H related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. H is the brother of E’s mother C. Therefore H is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of C. C is the father of E. B is the son of E. F is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of E, and E is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 45 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 21. New front rank = 22+3 = 25. Back rank = 45 − 25 + 1 = 21.

questions.stem: In a queue of 51 candidates, a candidate is 22th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 26. New front rank = 22+4 = 26. Back rank = 51 − 26 + 1 = 26.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹1900 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4260.61. Recover each cost separately: 1900×100/110 + 1900×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 28 and 42 hours. An outlet empties it in 42 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 28. Net rate = 1/28 + 1/42 − 1/42 = 1/28. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 72 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 3 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. Still-water speed = 12 km/h. Upstream speed = 12 − 3. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:6. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 7 months. A receives ₹259200 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 360000. Profit ratio is 108:42. Each ratio unit = ₹2400. Total = 150 × 2400.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹15000 earns ₹9000 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 21600. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 15000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 170 litres of pure milk. 34 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 108.8. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 170 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 31 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 61. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(31+1) − 29×31 = 61.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 18 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+18)/(x+18) = 3/2 gives x = 18. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 200 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. Relative speed = (57.6 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 12 m/s. Time = 200/12.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2100. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
